Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-3022", "title": "Brain Malformations", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Most brain malformations begin long before a baby is born."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Something damages the developing nervous system or causes it to develop abnormally."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "In other cases, exposure to certain medicines , infections , or radiation during pregnancy interferes with brain development."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Parts of the brain may be missing, abnormally small or large, or not fully developed."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "In many cases, treatment only helps with symptoms."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It may include antiseizure medicines, shunts to drain fluid from the brain, and physical therapy."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There are head malformations that do not involve the brain."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Craniofacial disorders are the result of abnormal growth of soft tissue and bones in the face and head."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It's common for new babies to have slightly uneven heads, but parents should watch the shape of their baby's head for possible problems."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6159", "title": "Psoriatic Arthritis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Psoriasis is a skin disease that causes itchy or sore patches of thick, red skin with silvery scales."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You usually get them on your elbows, knees, scalp, back, face, palms and feet, but they can show up on other parts of your body."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Some people with psoriasis have psoriatic arthritis."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It causes pain, stiffness, and swelling of the joints."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It is often mild, but can sometimes be serious and affect many joints."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The joint and skin problems don't always happen at the same time."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Your doctor will do a physical exam and imaging tests to diagnose psoriatic arthritis."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "There is no cure, but medicines can help control inflammation and pain."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "In rare cases, you might need surgery to repair or replace damaged joints."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3898", "title": "Rickets", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Rickets causes soft, weak bones in children."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It usually occurs when they do not get enough vitamin D , which helps growing bones absorb the minerals calcium and phosphorous."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can also happen when calcium or phosphorus levels are too low."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your child might not get enough vitamin D if he or she: Has dark skin Spends too little time outside Has on sunscreen all the time when out of doors Doesn't eat foods containing vitamin D because of lactose intolerance or a strict vegetarian diet Is breastfed without receiving vitamin D supplements Can't make or use vitamin D because of a medical disorder such as celiac disease In addition to dietary rickets, children can get an inherited form of the disease."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Symptoms include bone pain or tenderness, impaired growth, and deformities of the bones and teeth."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Your child's doctor uses lab and imaging tests to make the diagnosis."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Treatment is replacing the calcium, phosphorus, or vitamin D that are lacking in the diet."}]}, {"id": "MLP-2737", "title": "Tay-Sachs Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Tay-Sachs disease is a rare, inherited disease."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is a type of lipid metabolism disorder ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It causes too much of a fatty substance to build up in the brain."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "This buildup destroys nerve cells, causing mental and physical problems."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Infants with Tay-Sachs disease appear to develop normally for the first few months of life."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Then mental and physical abilities decline."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The child becomes blind, deaf, and unable to swallow."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Muscles begin to waste away and paralysis sets in."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Even with the best of care, children with Tay-Sachs disease usually die by age 4."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The cause is a gene mutation which is most common in Eastern European Ashkenazi Jews."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "To get the disease, both parents must have the gene."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If they do, there is a 25% chance of the child having the disease."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "A blood test and prenatal tests can check for the gene or the disease."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Medicines and good nutrition can help some symptoms."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-82", "title": "Lupus", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Lupus is a chronic (long-lasting) type of autoimmune disease ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Autoimmune diseases happen when your immune system attacks healthy cells and tissues by mistake."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It can also damage many parts of the body, including the joints, skin, kidneys, heart, lungs, and brain."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are several types of lupus: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the most common type."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It can be mild or severe and can affect many parts of the body."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It causes a rash or sores, usually after your skin is exposed to sunlight ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The two major types of cutaneous lupus are discoid lupus and subacute cutaneous lupus."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Drug-induced lupus is caused by a reaction to some medicines."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The symptoms may start 3 to 6 months after starting the medicine."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The symptoms usually go away when you stop taking the medicine."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Neonatal lupus, which is rare, affects newborns."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It is caused by certain antibodies that are passed from the pregnant mother to the fetus."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Researchers are studying what might cause or trigger the disease, such as: Genetics Environmental factors, such as viral infections , sunlight, certain medicines, and smoking Problems with the immune system Who is more likely to get lupus?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Anyone can get lupus, but women get it much more often than men."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Lupus is more common in African Americans than in White people."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It is also more common in people of American Indian and Asian descent."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "African American and Hispanic women are more likely to have severe forms of lupus."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Lupus can have many symptoms, and they differ from person to person."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Some of the more common ones are: Arthritis , causing painful and swollen joints and morning stiffness Fever Fatigue or feeling tired often Red rash , most often on the face (also called the \"butterfly rash\") Chest pain when taking a deep breath Hair loss Pale or purple fingers or toes, from cold and stress ( Raynaud phenomenon ) Sensitivity to the sun Swelling in legs or around eyes Mouth ulcers Swollen glands Headache and dizziness Confusion and memory problems Symptoms may come and go."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "When you are having symptoms, it is called a flare."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Lupus causes inflammation throughout your body."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "This can cause problems in your organs, including: Kidney damage (lupus nephritis)."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Heart problems , including inflammation in the heart (myocarditis), heart valves , or lining of the heart muscle ( pericarditis )."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Inflammation of blood vessels ( vasculitis )."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Blood clots Inflammation of the tissue that surrounds the lungs ( pleurisy )."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Some people with lupus may be more likely to develop other conditions, such as coronary artery disease (CAD) and atherosclerosis ."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There is no specific test for lupus, and it's often mistaken for other diseases that cause similar symptoms."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "So it may take a while to get a diagnosis."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "To find out if you have lupus, your health care provider: Will ask about your symptoms, medical history, and family health history Will do a complete physical exam May order blood tests, such as ANA (antinuclear antibody) , antibodies, complete blood count , and complement tests May order other tests, such as urine tests May do biopsies : Skin biopsy (looking at skin samples under a microscope) Kidney biopsy (looking at tissue from your kidney under a microscope) What are the treatments for lupus?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "There is no cure for lupus, but medicines and lifestyle changes can help control it."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "People with lupus often need to see different providers."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "You will most likely have a primary care provider and a rheumatologist (a doctor who specializes in autoimmune and other diseases of the bones, joints, and muscles)."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Which other specialists you may need depend on how lupus affects your body."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "For example, if lupus is damaging your heart or blood vessels, you would see a cardiologist (a doctor who specializes in heart diseases)."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Your primary care provider should coordinate care between all of your other providers and treat other problems as they come up."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "You and your primary care provider will develop a treatment plan to fit your needs."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "You will both review the plan often to make sure that it is working."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "You should report new symptoms to your provider right away so that your treatment plan can be changed, if needed."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "The goals of a treatment plan are to: Prevent flares Treat flares when they occur Reduce organ damage and other problems Improve your quality of life Treatments may include drugs to: Reduce fever, swelling, and pain Reduce inflammation in your body Prevent or reduce flares Reduce or prevent damage to joints Suppress (lower) the activity of your immune system Newer medicines are now available for some types of lupus, including lupus that affects the kidneys."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "These medicines work by targeting specific parts of the immune system."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Besides taking medicines for lupus, you may need to take medicines for problems that are related to lupus such as high cholesterol , high blood pressure , or infections."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Alternative and complementary therapies are therapies that are not part of standard treatments."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Some people try alternative and complementary therapies to improve their lupus symptoms."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "But research has not clearly shown whether these treatments may help or treat lupus."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Talk to your provider before trying any new treatments."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Researchers are also studying treatments, such as CAR-T cell therapy , for lupus that hasn't improved with other medicines."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "New treatments like this are usually only available by joining a research study, until they're approved for general use."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "It is important to take an active role in your treatment."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "It helps to learn more about lupus - being able to spot the warning signs of a flare can help you prevent the flare or make the symptoms less severe."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "It is also important to find ways to cope with the stress of having lupus."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Exercising and finding ways to relax may make it easier for you to cope."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases"}]}]
